title: Can you move between the conversation and other agents inside one terminal?
body: The settled Ctrl-] menu offers detach, take, release and interrupt. The prototype assumed you could also jump from Coordination's conversation straight into a worker that is waiting on you, and back again. Options: (A) Yes. The Ctrl-] menu also lists the conversation and every agent, with the agents waiting on you first, and choosing one moves this terminal there. Leaving the conversation this way counts as leaving it: your unsent text is saved and delivery resumes. The status line comes with you. (B) No. One attach per terminal: to look at another agent you detach and run `asmai attach`, or open another terminal.
try: Scenario 'Step into a worker', steps 3 and 10.
rec: A. Answering a worker's native prompt is then a couple of keystrokes from the conversation, and the status line already shows where you are and whose input you hold. `asmai attach <agent>` still works in a second terminal.
options: A: Ctrl-] menu switches this terminal between the conversation and any agent

title: What happens if the conversation is open in two terminals at once?
body: For example, your laptop is still attached when you run `asmai` from your phone over SSH. Two places typing into one conversation would be competing human input. Options: (A) The newest attach takes the conversation. The older terminal shows a one-line notice and stays as an observer, and any unsent text there is saved as if you had left. The same applies to an agent whose input you hold: a newer `take` from another terminal moves your hold there. (B) The second attach is refused until the first detaches, with `--force` doing A. (C) Both terminals can type.
rec: A. The usual reason for a second attach is that you have moved, and the old terminal may be unreachable. Saving the old terminal's unsent text keeps the rule you chose for unsent text. C breaks the single-input-owner contract.
options: A: newest attach takes over; the old terminal observes and its unsent text is saved
B: refuse the second attach unless --force

title: Can you interrupt Coordination while it is on an automated turn?
body: You may want Coordination's attention now while it is routing a handoff. In the provider's screen, Esc interrupts the running turn. Options: (A) Yes. Your keys always reach the conversation. An interrupted automated turn counts as interrupted: after Coordination has answered you, the daemon nudges it again, and it re-reads the same messages (reads are idempotent by message ID) and checks its own recorded `asmai` calls before acting again, so nothing is blindly repeated. (B) No. During automated turns the attach client holds Esc back; you type ahead, and the provider queues your message until the turn ends.
rec: A. The conversation is yours, and a queued message can sit behind a long automated turn. Repeat nudges, idempotent reads and recorded calls are already part of the work-state contract, so an interruption needs no new mechanism. The feasibility probe saw no Interrupt hook from Claude Code, so recognizing an interrupted Claude turn becomes a qualification case.
options: A: yes; the interrupted automated turn is re-nudged and checked, never blindly repeated
B: no; my message waits until the automated turn ends

title: How is a Lavish page tied to the decision it asks about?
body: The daemon collects Lavish answers, so it has to know which decision version and which question each answer belongs to. Options: (A) Structured questions plus optional content. The requesting agent submits its questions as structured data with the decision request (id, title, body, options, recommendation). The daemon renders them in one standard layout, keyed to the decision version, and can tell when every question has an answer. The agent may attach its own content above the questions, such as a prototype, a diff or a report. Comments and annotations you leave anywhere on the page are journaled word for word and routed with the answers. (B) Free-form pages. The agent writes the whole page and keys its questions by convention; the daemon only serves it and records whatever comes back. (C) Daemon-rendered questions only, with no agent content on the page.
try: This board has that shape: a prototype above structured questions.
rec: A. Keys from the daemon make every answer attributable to exactly one decision version, and agents keep room for prototypes and reviews. C cannot show a prototype or a diff, and B leaves the keying to each agent's care.
options: A: structured questions rendered by the daemon, plus optional agent content
